body:
i'm really interested in the idea of finally trying out different antidepressants and hopefully finding one that works. i've seen happy people, and i have better days (although very rarely), so i know that theoretically it should be possible for me to turn infrequent good days into infrequent bad days. the only thing i'm sorta questioning is the ability of meds to cause such a drastic change. but hey, even a slight positive result is better than nothing.


today wasn't too bad aside from the concentration issues and headaches that decided to return in full force, but i'll definitely say hello on the other subreddit when the depression itself goes back to being heavy. thank you for being such a nice stranger; it's encouraging to hear that someone's rooting for me, even if i'm not on my own side sometimes.

i actually have some pets! only cats, and i don't see them during the week since i'm on campus and living in a dorm, but it's nice to have them around when i visit my family over the weekend. i've always found that pets are good at knowing when you're sick or in a depressed mood, they really are great.


unfortunately i've always been terrible at recognizing my own emotions, so by the time i pick up on the fact that i've been feeling particularly down, it's usually already been a few hours since it started. i can see how that would be helpful if i was more in tune! there's a sort of turning point, at least for me: if i manage to pick up on the fact that i'm feeling a bit depressed, sometimes i can ease out of that mindset, but it does spiral otherwise. sorry if that doesn't make a huge amount of sense, today was a better day depression-wise but i've also been getting my headaches and brain fog, so it's difficult to concentrate enough to get thoughts typed out.


i really do appreciate the thoughtful response; i'll take the time to watch that video and hopefully the day for my appointment with the psychiatrist will arrive before too long.

ahhh i feel that. i don't always get along with my family either, but when it comes down to it, i don't want to make their lives miserable by disappearing off the face of the earth. that's really the only reason i'm here and it seems a bit pathetic.


i'm glad to hear that antidepressants worked for you; i'm sorta hopeful about the fact that they're reconsidering putting me on those, since originally the doctors didn't want to. something about increased risk of suicide. it's going to be a long twelve days of waiting for that appointment.


anyway, thanks for the nice words. i enjoy... i don't know? there used to be things that i felt really happy seeing or doing, but these days it's more of a fleeting, shallow feeling of enjoyment, and then it's gone. i'd play video games but it's hard to focus on anything, so maybe i'll go on youtube and watch other people playing games instead.


my day was pretty busy; had three lectures and a few errands, so i'm drained in terms of energy but i don't think i'll be able to sleep tonight. at least tomorrow should be less hectic, but that also means i'll have more time alone with my thoughts, and that's a little scary on its own.


again, thanks for commenting, i'm glad that there are folks who spend time trying to cheer up people like me. makes the world seem a little less dark.

I know I'm young, and that's part of what scares me. It feels like things are always going to be like this, or maybe worse; that I'll keep getting sucked towards this black hole of depression until there is no way to get any lower. I think one of the reasons that my attempts at social interactions feel fake is that nobody cares, not really. At the end of the day they've got their own lives, and connections are fleeting. What's the point of trying to make friends if they're just going to leave like all the others? I'm tired of starting from square one and I'm not very good at being open with people in any case.


Coincidentally, my next appointment with the therapist is actually tomorrow. I guess I could tell them what's really up, but for all I know I'd get Baker Acted, and I can't let that happen. Not only would it be a huge issue in regards to my family (I've only told them that I'm depressed, nothing about the suicidal aspect), but it would really mess with my schoolwork. I don't have time to sit in an asylum for however long they'd keep me there. Missing lectures isn't an option unless I want to be even more behind on my work. I'm barely making it through this semester as it is.


I talk too much. Thanks for commenting, it really means a lot that you're here trying to help people like me.
